gaps.sentence: All the tickets ___ (sell) within an hour of going on sale.
gaps.explanation: Past simple passive: were + sold. 'All the tickets' takes a plural verb.

gaps.sentence: The tickets ___ at the door from seven o'clock.
gaps.explanation: Modal passive: can be + collected. The tickets are collected by the buyers.

gaps.sentence: The finalists ___ (interview) live on air as we speak.
gaps.explanation: 'As we speak' demands the present continuous passive: are being + interviewed.

gaps.sentence: The missing manuscripts ___ (find) — the search is officially over.
gaps.explanation: Present perfect passive: have/has been + past participle. The result matters now.

gaps.sentence: The fault ___ by the time the auditor arrived.
gaps.explanation: The fixing preceded the arrival: past perfect passive had been + fixed.

gaps.sentence: The recipe ___ (pass down) from generation to generation.
gaps.hint: continuing relevance from past to now
gaps.explanation: Present perfect passive: has been + passed down; the process links past and present.

gaps.sentence: The village ___ (reach) by road until 1962; only mules could make the climb.
gaps.explanation: 'Until 1962' describes a past state of affairs: could not be + past participle.

gaps.sentence: The whole street ___ when the gas main burst.
gaps.explanation: The street was evacuated by others: past necessity had to be + evacuated.
